question.title: Two Sum
question.description:
# Two Sum

Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

## Requirements
- You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution
- You may not use the same element twice
- Return the answer in any order

## Constraints
- 2 <= nums.length <= 10^4
- -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
- -10^9 <= target <= 10^9
- Only one valid answer exists

## Examples

### Example 1:
```
Input: nums = [2,7,11,15], target = 9
Output: [0,1]
Explanation: Because nums[0] + nums[1] == 9, we return [0, 1].
```

### Example 2:
```
Input: nums = [3,2,4], target = 6
Output: [1,2]
```

### Example 3:
```
Input: nums = [3,3], target = 6
Output: [0,1]
```

## Follow-up
Can you come up with an algorithm that is less than O(n^2) time complexity?

followUpQuestions.questionText: What is the time and space complexity of your solution?
followUpQuestions.answer:
Optimal solution using hash map:
• Time: O(n) - single pass through array
• Space: O(n) - hash map storage

Brute force:
• Time: O(n^2) - nested loops
• Space: O(1) - no extra space

followUpQuestions.questionText: Can you solve it without using extra space?
followUpQuestions.answer:
Candidates might mention:
• Two-pointer approach (requires sorted array)
• Would need to sort first (O(n log n))
• Trade-off between time and space

Note: Hash map approach is preferred for unsorted array

followUpQuestions.questionText: What if the array was sorted? Would you change your approach?
followUpQuestions.answer:
With sorted array:
• Two-pointer approach becomes optimal
• Time: O(n), Space: O(1)
• Start from both ends, move pointers based on sum

Shows understanding of:
• Different approaches for different constraints
• Time-space trade-offs
